hypotheses.statement: The incident was caused by an expired TLS certificate on payments-gateway.internal, which caused the checkout-api payments-connector to fail TLS handshakes, leading to 502 errors and high latency on POST /v2/checkout/submit.

observed_facts.statement: Alert checkout-api-error-ratio fired at 09:12:03Z, observing a 5xx ratio of 0.184 for POST /v2/checkout/submit.
Alert checkout-api-latency fired at 09:14:41Z, reporting p99 latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit rose to 10400ms.
Release 2026.5.14-a was deployed to production at 09:09:52Z, containing copy edits to email templates and a CSV export library dependency bump.
Rollback of checkout-api to 2026.5.13-c completed at 10:04:18Z, after the 5xx ratio had already recovered at 09:58:10Z.
At 09:11:47Z, checkout-api payments-connector began experiencing repeated outbound TLS handshake failures to payments-gateway.internal:8443 due to an expired certificate.
At 09:12:02Z, checkout-api POST /v2/checkout/submit began returning 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted retries.
At 09:57:55Z, checkout-api payments-connector outbound TLS handshakes to payments-gateway.internal:8443 succeeded again and the error rate returned to baseline.
A sampled trace shows POST /v2/checkout/submit took 10402ms, with the payments.authorize span taking 10388ms and terminating in a client timeout error.
A responder attributed the incident to the release at 09:17:22Z.
A responder disputed the release attribution at 09:23:05Z, pointing to TLS failures and the release not touching the submit path.
The payments-gateway team reported at 09:59:40Z that their leaf certificate expired at 09:11:40Z and was rotated at 09:57:50Z, with no known owner for the renewal automation.
INC-7742 was opened at 09:15:00Z with severity 1, titled 'Checkout submit failing for all customers', with no impact field filled.
INC-7742 was marked resolved with a resolution note stating only 'rolled back and recovered', not mentioning the certificate rotation.

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or configuration records identifying the owner/automation responsible for renewing the payments-gateway.internal TLS certificate.
open_questions.question: Who owns the renewal automation for the payments-gateway.internal TLS certificate, and why did it fail?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Records estimating customer impact (e.g., failed transactions, affected users).
open_questions.question: What was the customer and business impact of the incident?

summary: The checkout-5xx incident was caused by an expired TLS certificate on the payments-gateway.internal service, leading to TLS handshake failures in the checkout-api payments-connector. This resulted in 502 errors and high latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit requests. The incident began shortly after a deployment, but evidence shows the deployment did not contain changes relevant to the failing path. Recovery occurred after the certificate was rotated, independent of a rollback that was executed after the system had already recovered.

timeline.statement: checkout-api payments-connector began experiencing TLS handshake failures due to expired certificate.
checkout-api payments-connector TLS handshakes succeeded again; error rate returned to baseline.
